territorial_scope.description: Applies to New York State and the government agencies defined in section 501(3) of the State Technology Law, including state, local, school and public authority bodies.

evidence.quote: The People of the State of New York, represented in Senate and Assembly, do enact as follows:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Requires New York State government agencies to publish lists of automated decision-making tools, complete impact assessments for tools used with meaningful human review, and submit them to the governor and legislature before implementation. Article V takes effect one year after enactment.
summary.long: Adds Article V to the State Technology Law. Government agencies (state and local bodies, school districts, SUNY, CUNY, public authorities) using automated decision-making tools must publish a list of them by 30 December after section one takes effect, then annually. Where a tool is used with ongoing meaningful human review, agencies must complete signed impact assessments at least every two years and before material changes, and submit them to the governor and legislative leaders at least 30 days before implementation; assessments are published with permitted redactions. If an assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, use must cease. A state office maintains an inventory on the open data website, and agencies must report existing tools to the legislature within one year. Education Law sections 115, 2510, 2585, 2588 and 3013 and Civil Service Law section 80(10) provide that use of such tools shall not affect collective bargaining rights or result in employee discharge, displacement or transfer of duties. Section one takes effect one year after enactment; the other sections take effect immediately. The text sets no penalties.

notes: No legal_basis or repeal is stated. Sections 4–9 use 'artificial intelligence systems as defined by section one hundred three-e of the state technology law', but § 103-e is not in this text. § 103-f refers to 'the office' without defining it and uses 'artificial intelligence inventory' in subd. 4 while the title uses 'automated decision-making tool inventory'. Timing is unclear: § 10 makes Article V (§ 1) take effect one year after enactment, yet § 502 and § 103-f key deadlines to when 'this section' takes effect, and § 3 runs from 'the effective date of this section'. Drafting errors: § 2588(b)(ii) reads 'to and artificial'; § 9(c) contains bracketed '[an] such'. Section 10 says § 9 expires and is repealed with the civil service subdivision, and that subdivision's expiry date is not stated in this text.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff found that changes legal treatment of a person, entity or service. The numbers present (the 30 December publication deadlines, the one-year effective-date period in section 3, the two-year impact assessment cycle, the thirty days before implementation in section 504(1), the sixty days before the annual publication in section 103-f, and the one-year period in section 10) are procedural time limits and are coded as events, not thresholds.
